defendant: Luke Patrick, Jr.; United States of America; Sunnova Asset Portfolio 4 LLC; Sunnova Management LLC; Midland Funding LLC
description:
SUPERIOR COURT OF NEW JERSEY
CHANCERY DIVISION - SALEM COUNTY
DOCKET NO.
F-013926-25
SHERIFF NO.
26000323
PLAINTIFF -
JPMorgan Chase Bank, National Association
DEFENDANT -
Luke Patrick, Jr.; United States of America; Sunnova Asset Portfolio 4 LLC; Sunnova Management LLC; Midland Funding LLC
By virtue of a Writ of Execution in the above stated action to me directed, I shall expose for sale at public venue at the Salem County Courthouse, situated at No. 92 Market Street, in the City of Salem, New Jersey on
Monday,
December 14, 2026
at
2 o’clock
in the afternoon, ALL the following lot, tract or parcel of land and premises, situate, lying and being in the Township of Mannington , in the County of Salem and State of New Jersey, bounded and described as follows:
Municipality:
Mannington
County of Salem
State of New Jersey
Street and Street No.: 233 Old Kings Hwy Mannington, NJ 08079 a/k/a 233 Old Kings Highway Mannington, NJ 08079
Tax Block and Lot No.: Block 51, Lot 5
Dimensions of Lot (approximately): Tract No.1 129.96ft x 85ft x 129.96ft x 85ft, Tract No.2 85ft x 75ft x 85 ft x 75ft
Nearest Cross Street: Approximately 358.76ft to nearest cross street known as Newell Road
A full legal description of the premises can be found in the offices of the County Clerk in Deed Book 3120 at Page 716 and the Sheriff of Salem County.
The approximate amount of the judgment to be satisfied by said sale is the sum of $180,650.04 together with the costs of this sale.
The approximate upset price is $195,090.75.
The upset price may be subject to further Orders of additional sums.
Occupancy Status: Borrower Occupied
Pursuant to a municipal Tax Search dated October 4, 2026.
Subject to:
2026 4th quarter taxes due 11/1/2026, $1,391.00 OPEN
2027 1st quarter taxes due 2/1/2027, $1,406.40 OPEN
2027 2nd quarter taxes due 5/1/2027, $1,406.39 OPEN
Terms of Sale: 20% of bid in cash, certified check or cashiers check from the successful bidder upon conclusion of sale. The Sheriff’s Office cash limit is $1,000.00 The balance is due within 30 days of the date of sale.
Surplus Money:
If after the sale and satisfaction of the mortgage debt, including costs and expenses, there remains any surplus money, the money will be deposited into the Superior Court Trust Fund and any person claiming the surplus, or any part thereof, may file a motion pursuant to the Court Rules 4:64-3 and 4:57-2 stating the nature and extent of that person’s claim and asking for an order directing payment of the surplus money. The Sheriff or other person conducting the sale will have information regarding the surplus, if any.
The Sheriff reserves the right to adjourn the sale without further notice through publication.
Hill Wallack LLP
, Attorneys for Plaintiff
Charles M. Miller, Sheriff
